title: Canary containment incident: lessons, runbook codification, and rollback automation
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: A canary rollout of model v2.3.0 triggered a slow drift in output latency and a 7% increase in 95th percentile tail latency for a subset of customers. Traffic was automatically shifted per rollout policy but a mismatch in shadow vs canary KV-cache keying surfaced only after partial promotion, leading to degraded throughput on two dedicated pools. This ticket captures the incident chronology, root causes, concrete runbook changes, telemetry gaps, and follow-up automation to prevent recurrence.

Why this matters: The event exposed a gap between shadow validation and canary promotion checks: shadow traffic did not encounter the same KV eviction pattern because shadow instances used a different cache key prefix configuration. After promotion, cache churn increased causing GPU memory pressure and queuing, which amplified latency for latency-sensitive tenants and triggered downstream timeouts in upstream callers.

Scope & impact: Scope limited to 2 dedicated GPU pools in us-west-2. Approximately 3% of production requests experienced transient 5-15s latency spikes during peak. No data leakage or correctness regressions observed. Billing exposure estimated low but SLO violations recorded for one high-traffic customer.

Timeline (high level):
- 2025-02-17 15:02 PST: Canary rollout (10% traffic) started for model v2.3.0 via runtime-1.20 rollout policy.
- 2025-02-17 15:18 PST: Ops alert - surge in queue depth on pool-redwood-12.
- 2025-02-17 15:25 PST: Automated rollback attempted but failed to trigger due to stale promotion token in rollout controller.
- 2025-02-17 15:42 PST: Manual rollback initiated; traffic reverted to previous model at 15:47 PST.
- 2025-02-18 10:00 PST: Post-incident triage and initial hypothesis formed (KV-cache collision + promotion token race).

Root causes (synthesized):
1) KV-cache keying mismatch between shadow harness and canary runtime instances (configuration drift).
2) Rollout controller token state machine allowed a stale token to suppress an automated abort path (race with autoscaler and rollout commit).
3) Telemetry contract gap: shadow telemetry did not capture per-key eviction counters or per-pool memory pressure metrics used by autoscaler heuristics.
4) Canary thresholds were tuned to aggregate latency (p50/p90) and did not account for isolated pool degradation signals.

Decisions & trade-offs considered:
- Option A: Tighten shadow parity by sharing cache-keying config with shadow. Pros: higher fidelity pre-promotion signal. Cons: slightly reduces isolation between testing and prod caches.
- Option B: Add synthetic litmus tests that intentionally stress cache churn in shadow before promotion. Pros: finds cache-sensitive regressions; Cons: adds test flakiness and increases test runtime.
- Option C: Harden rollout controller to surface token state and to include a fast abort path triggered by pool-specific hysteresis. Pros: stronger automatic protection; Cons: added controller complexity.
Decision: Implement a combination of A and C (immediate parity + rollout controller guardrails); schedule B as a follow-on experiment for coverage.

Runbook changes (to be codified):
- Canary pre-promotion checklist now includes explicit config parity verification step: verify KV_CACHE_PREFIX, shard mapping, and eviction policy are identical between shadow and canary instances.
- Add explicit per-pool memory_pressure and eviction_rate thresholds to the SLO-based canary guardrail.
- Fast-abort criteria added: if any dedicated pool exceeds eviction_rate threshold or p95 latency rises > 40% relative to baseline for more than 2 minutes, the rollout controller must abort and initiate immediate rollback.
- Promotion token workflow enhanced: rollout agents must refresh promotion tokens on autoscaler events; tokens expire after 60s to avoid stale state.
- Post-rollback stabilization window: 15 minutes of synthetic traffic run on the promoted baseline before allowing reattempts.

Telemetry & observability work:
- New metrics to emit from runtime: per-pool eviction_rate, cache_hit_ratio by prefix, gpu_mem_pressure_percent, and per-request kv_misses.
- Dashboards: Add a "Canary Containment" dashboard showing per-pool heatmaps, eviction_rate trends, and rollout token state.
- Alerts: Create a dedicated SLO alert that triggers when eviction_rate exceeds threshold on any pool with canary traffic.

Automation & engineering tasks (high level):
- Implement rollout controller fixes (ENG-420010) to fast-abort on pool signals and rotate promotion tokens on autoscaler events.
- Add a config-sync utility (ENG-420011) that verifies shadow vs canary config parity for cache and shard mapping prior to promotion.
- Instrument runtime to export eviction_rate and gpu_mem_pressure (runtime-1.20-eviction-metrics PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1342).
- Add synthetic litmus harness for KV churn to the shadow test suite (ENG-420025).

Action items (concrete, assigned):
- "Adrian Patel: implement rollout controller token expiry and fast-abort logic" (estimate 3).
- "Priya Rao: add eviction_rate and gpu_mem_pressure metrics to runtime and expose via Prometheus" (estimate 5).
- "Sofia Morales: author canary pre-promotion checklist and add to Console rollout UI" (estimate 2).
- "Maya Chen: coordinate customer comms and open a customer-facing incident summary" (estimate 1).
- "Infra SRE: run a controlled stress test on staging dedicated pools with synthetic KV churn" (collab).

Notes on verification & acceptance criteria:
- Unit and integration tests for rollout controller token expiry + abort path in CI.
- Shadow parity checker must produce zero diffs for cache configuration on 3 consecutive runs in staging before enabling parity enforcement in prod.
- Synthetic KV churn experiment must reproduce eviction_rate > 70% of production observed during incident in staging.

Links & artifacts:
- Incident Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01INCIDENTS/p1676700000000
- Runtime PR for eviction metrics: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1342
- Draft runbook changes (Confluence): https://company.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/Canary+Containment+Runbook+Draft
- Rollout controller quickfix PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/controller/pull/418

Open questions:
- Should shadow environments share persistent caches with production read-only mode for higher fidelity? (security & isolation trade-offs)
- What is the right per-pool eviction_rate threshold—should it be absolute or dynamically computed relative to baseline?

Follow-up timeline:
- By 2025-03-07: rollout controller token fix merged and smoke-tested in staging.
- By 2025-03-14: runtime metrics merged and dashboards created.
- By 2025-03-21: synthetic KV churn experiments executed and threshold tuning completed.

Longer-term ideas:
- Explore per-tenant canary throttling (reduce canary percentage for tenants with sensitive latency SLOs).
- Evaluate an automated "circuit-breaker" for model swaps that can redirect heavy-tail traffic to smaller-context variants until caches warm.
- Consider a rollout simulation harness that replays historical traffic into shadow with production cache state to catch cache-keying regressions earlier.
